label: Local-first software
scope: Principle: local-first software keeps the user's data primarily on the user's own device, keeps working offline, and treats sync or collaboration with other devices and people as optional and under the user's control. The test is whether local data ownership, offline use or sync is the project's main point or just an implementation detail. Most desktop software keeps files on the machine; that alone does not make it local-first, and neither does calling itself local-first, being self-hosted, or running a local AI model. A project whose main purpose is something else (an assistant, an agent manager, analytics, media) is off topic even if its data stays local. Illustrations only (not exhaustive): on topic are things like sync engines, CRDT or replication libraries, offline-first storage, and apps built on them; off topic are things like a server product that you self-host, or a tool that just runs on your machine without a local-data or sync story. When the description is ambiguous, read the README and apply the principle.
